topics.description: Physical processes in which a substance changes from one state of matter to another due to changes in temperature, pressure, or other conditions.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The Ehrenfest (EE-ren-fest) classification system for these events organizes them based on the degree  of their order parameters. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these transitions between states of matter such as melting or freezing.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Phase changes can be plotted on a phase diagram. At this point on the diagram a substance exists as  a solid, liquid, and gas.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] A cold finger is used in a process that extracts impurities during this phase transition that carbon  dioxide demonstrates below the triple point.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer the following about phase transitions, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: This phase transition occurs when a solid transitions to a liquid. Water has a value of 0 celsius for this transition.

parts.label: B
parts.question: This phase transition occurs when a solid, such as dry ice, transitions directly into a gas.

parts.label: C
parts.question: At this point, solid, liquid, and gas phases can exist at the same time. By definition, the temperature at which  this point occurs is 0.01 celsius.

topics.description: The point on Earth's surface directly above an earthquake's underground focus or hypocenter.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The speed of these waves equals the square root of the ratio between the medium’s modulus of rigidity and its density. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these transverse waves whose “shadow zone” results from their inability to pass through liquid.
parts.answer: S waves [or secondary waves or shear waves; prompt on seismic waves or body waves; do NOT accept or prompt on “surface waves”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] The S-wave shadow zone reveals the liquid nature of this layer of the Earth. According to dynamo theory, Earth’s magnetic field results from the motion of this layer below the mantle.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] The difference in arrival time between S waves and P waves allows seismologists to triangulate this location, the point on Earth’s surface that lies directly above where an earthquake originates.
parts.answer: epicenter [or epicentre or epicentrum; do NOT accept or prompt on “focus” or “hypocenter”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: One of these occurred on Good Friday in 1964 in Alaska, and a devastating one of these in 1906 caused days of fires in San Francisco. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name these events in which tectonic plates interact, causing the release of seismic waves. They often cause the ground to shake and destroy buildings.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Earthquakes' intensity is measured by this logarithmic scale, which has largely been replaced by the moment magnitude scale. Earthquakes with a value of above 7.0 on this scale are considered "major".

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] This term is used to describe the point on the Earth's surface directly above where an earthquake started. It is contrasted with the hypocenter.

topics.description: The brain is the central organ of the nervous system, located inside the skull and responsible for information processing, memory, and control of many bodily functions.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: One region of this organ contains a part of dentate granule cells called mossy fibers. In this organ, Schwann cells create a layer of myelin over a certain type of cell. The cavity in which this organ resides is filled with (*) cerebrospinal fluid to protect it and remove waste. Processes like breathing are controlled in this organ's namesake stem. For 10 points, name this organ inside the skull in which neurons are used to store information

parts.label: L
parts.question: This organ contains several regions called "lobes", including the frontal and parietal ones. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this organ located inside the skull, the center of the body's nervous system.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] This part of the brain derives its name from the Greek word for "seahorse". It is responsible for converting short-term to long-term memories, and humans contain two, one for each side of the brain.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Two other parts of the brain, Broca's area and Wernicke's (VER-nick-uh’s) area, are responsible for this ability, and damage to those areas can cause aphasia, in which they are unable to perform this ability successfully, instead producing meaningless gibberish or repeated syllables.
parts.answer: speech [or language or talking or really anything that refers to flapping your vocal cords and making sound come out of your mouth hole]

topics.description: A method of defining or performing a computation or process in terms of itself or smaller instances of itself, typically with a terminating base case.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Two basic operations used to modify this structure are “push” and “pop.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this “last in, first out” data structure. An “overflow” of these structures names a common  error in Java.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Stack overflow can commonly occur with this type of computation. This operation involves a  function calling itself.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Unlike heaps, stacks can be used to store local examples of these entities. Commonly used symbols  for these entities include the letters x and y.

topics.description: Energy associated with an object's position in a force field or with the configuration of a system, including gravitational and elastic forms.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: For a conservative force, work equals the negative change in this quantity. One-half times the spring constant times displacement squared gives the elastic form of this quantity, which is stored in springs. A ball at the top of a hill has the (*) gravitational form of this property, which in general comes from the position of objects. For ten points, name this type of energy which is converted by motion into kinetic energy.
parts.answer: potential energy [prompt on energy by asking “What kind of energy?”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Around 1780, Joseph-Louis Lagrange [luh-GRAHNJ] reformulated classical mechanics. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [E] His formulation was based on a function called the Lagrangian [luh-GRAHN-jee-un], defined as kinetic energy minus this other type of energy that objects have due to their position.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [H] Performing this operation on the Lagrangian yields a quantity called “action.” This operation performed on power gives the change in energy.
parts.answer: time integral [or equivalents like integrating with respect to time; prompt on integral or equivalents]

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] Noether’s theorem holds that this quantity is conserved due to the Lagrangian’s symmetry under translations in space. Unlike kinetic energy, this quantity is conserved in inelastic collisions.

topics.description: The force per unit area exerted by Earth's atmosphere, commonly measured with a barometer and approximately 101 kilopascals at sea level.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The exponential atmosphere model predicts that this quantity decays exponentially, not linearly, with height. Devices that measure this quantity consist of a glass tube suspended in a reservoir, and consequently often measure it in (*) millimeters. Winds move in the direction where this quantity decreases, which is why storms often develop in areas where it’s low. For ten points, name this quantity that is approximately 101 kilopascals, or 1 atmosphere, at sea level.

parts.label: L
parts.question: These weather phenomena typically form over warm water. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name these weather phenomena rated from 1 to 5 on the Saffir–Simpson scale. They are classified as a 12 of the Beaufort scale.
parts.answer: hurricanes [accept cyclones or typhoons] [prompt tropical storms]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [M] This region of a hurricane is characterized by calm weather. It occurs in the center of tropical cyclones such as hurricanes.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [E] The lowest value of this quantity for a hurricane typically occurs in its eye. It is measured with a barometer.

topics.description: Methanol is the simplest alcohol, a toxic substance with the formula CH3OH used as an industrial solvent, fuel, and chemical feedstock.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These compounds can be selectively oxidized by either pyridinium chlorochromate or sodium dichromate depending on whether the desired product is an aldehyde or a carboxylic acid. One of these compounds is toxic because a dehydrogenase oxidizes it to produce formic acid instead of the intended product acetaldehyde. It is difficult to purify one of these compounds past 96% because it forms an (*) azeotrope with water during distillation. The primary ingredient in many disinfectants is a type of these compounds named “isopropyl.” For 10 points, name these compounds which contain an -OH group and include methanol and ethanol.
parts.answer: alcohols [accept hydroxyls, accept isopropyl alcohol, prompt on methanol or ethanol by asking “what more general class of compounds is that a part of”]

parts.label: L
parts.question: Though it is perhaps not its most famous application, formaldehyde is mainly used to make resins for products like particle board and laminate flooring. Answer these questions about its chemistry, for ten points each.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Formaldehyde is classified as this type of compound, along with benzene and sugar, because it contains carbon and is produced by cellular reactions.

parts.label: B
parts.question: Formaldehyde is synthesized industrially by the oxidation of this simplest alcohol with formula CH3OH [C-H-3-O-H].
parts.answer: methanol (accept methyl alcohol; accept wood alcohol)

parts.label: C
parts.question: Formaldehyde has traditionally been a major component of the fluid injected into a body during this process that fixes tissues and slows decomposition by microorganisms.

topics.description: A combination is a selection of objects from a group in which the order of selection does not matter.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The notation “N choose K” is often used to denote this mathematical concept. For ten points each,

parts.label: A
parts.question: Give this term for a selection of objects out of a group in which the order that the objects are chosen does not matter.

parts.label: B
parts.question: In this related concept symbolized with a P, the order in which the numbers are chosen does matter.

parts.label: C
parts.question: The formulas for both permutations and combinations involve factorials, in which an integer is multiplied by every positive integer less than it. The expression “n factorial” is written using this punctuation mark.

topics.description: A binomial coefficient, written as n choose k, counts the ways to select k items from n items.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Answer some questions about 4-digit numbers which contain the digits 7 and 8 exactly twice each, for 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] There are this many possible such numbers, equal to the value of 4 choose 2.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Two of the numbers, 7887 and 8778, are this kind of number which is the same written both forwards and backwards.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] All six numbers must be divisible by this smallest odd prime, because any number whose digits sum to a multiple of this number, like 12 or 39, must be divisible by this number.

topics.description: Visible atmospheric formations composed of condensed water droplets or ice crystals, including types such as stratus, cumulus, cirrus, mammatus, and nacreous clouds.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A type of these objects that form primarily near the poles are named “nacreous”. Mammatus and pileus are two types of these objects, and contrails are a man-made form created by jet engines. In the water cycle, these objects form after evaporation as water (*) condenses in the sky. Types of these objects include stratus, cumulus, and cirrus. For ten points, name these usually-white masses of water vapor in the sky.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: These objects may be "seeded" using a small pellet of silver iodide. Their unusual mammatus type is caused by strong updrafts, and these objects are formed when air temperature moves below the dew point in the (*) stratosphere. Rain, snow, and other precipitation are formed by the condensation of water vapor in, for 10 points, what large masses of air which may block out the sun?
parts.answer: clouds [prompt on storms before "mammatus" by asking "what physical objects comprise the storm?"; prompt on answers indicating rain or precipitation or similar before "mammatus" by asking "from what objects does the rain originate?"]
